## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The rule possesses extensive parallels across Buddhist monastic traditions. In Pali canonical Vinaya literature, exact parallels occur in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Sk 8), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (Sk 8), and both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra. Parallels in other Vinaya lineages are preserved in Chinese and Sanskrit, including the Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga texts of the Sarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Lokottaravāda traditions.

None of the retrieved secondary literature passages pertain to this Vinaya rule, as all search results represent false matches to homonymous abbreviations, specifically verse 8 of the *Sāṃkhyakārikā* and Tibetan enumerations of the eighty-four *mahāsiddhas*.
